title: What does APRA CPS 230 mean for staff training and capability?
description: CPS 230 has no training clause, but its people, controls, incident and continuity duties depend on staff capability. What applies as at September 2026.
shortAnswer: Prudential Standard CPS 230 Operational Risk Management, made by the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA), contains no explicit training requirement. It does require entities to manage risk from the actions or inactions of people, set standards for conduct and compliance, define senior manager responsibilities, record incidents and near misses, and maintain the capabilities, including access to people, needed to execute business continuity plans. Staff capability is how those duties are met and evidenced.
keyTakeaways: CPS 230 commenced on July 1, 2025. APRA remade it with targeted amendments released on April 30, 2026, and that version commences on July 1, 2026.
Non-significant financial institutions had business continuity requirements deferred to July 1, 2026, and pre-existing service provider contracts had until the earlier of renewal or July 1, 2026.
The standard names people as a source of operational risk and as a resource that critical operations and business continuity plans depend on.
Neither CPS 230 nor its practice guide CPG 230 uses the word training, so capability must be shown through roles, controls testing, incident handling and exercises.
Staff need to know two notification clocks: 72 hours for material operational risk incidents and 24 hours for disruptions to critical operations outside tolerance.
appliesTo: Authorised deposit-taking institutions (ADIs) and authorised banking NOHCs
General insurers, life companies and private health insurers
RSE licensees in respect of their business operations
Boards and senior managers accountable for operational risk, business continuity and service providers

sections.heading: Which version of CPS 230 applies, and from when?

blocks.text: CPS 230 first commenced on July 1, 2025, and a remade version with targeted amendments commences on July 1, 2026. APRA [announced](https://www.apra.gov.au/news-and-publications/apra-finalises-new-prudential-standard-on-operational-risk) in 2023 that the standard would commence from July 1, 2025, and [confirmed](https://www.apra.gov.au/news-and-publications/apra-provides-update-implementation-new-operational-risk-standard) that pre-existing service provider contracts would be covered from the earlier of the next renewal date or July 1, 2026.

The [2025 version](https://www.apra.gov.au/standards/cps-230-superseded) also deferred paragraphs 40, 41 and 43 to 46 (the business continuity requirements) for non-significant financial institutions until July 1, 2026. On April 30, 2026 APRA released final targeted amendments that introduce limited exemptions from specific contractual requirements for certain categories of service providers, together with an updated CPG 230 and register template, all commencing July 1, 2026 ([APRA operational risk page](https://www.apra.gov.au/operational-risk-management)). Paragraph numbers on this page refer to the [current standard](https://www.apra.gov.au/standards/cps-230) as at September 2026.

blocks.title: Paragraph numbering changed
blocks.text: Paragraph numbers differ between the 2025 and 2026 versions. For example, the 72 hour incident notification is paragraph 32 in the 2026 version, while it was paragraph 33 in the 2025 version. Cite the version in force when documenting obligations.

sections.heading: Where does CPS 230 depend on staff capability?

blocks.text: CPS 230 refers to people as both a cause of operational risk and a resource to be managed. Paragraph 12 requires an entity to manage operational risks that may result from "inadequate or failed internal processes or systems, the actions or inactions of people or external drivers and events". Paragraph 11(a) requires it to "set and maintain appropriate standards for conduct and compliance".

items: **Paragraph 20:** the Board must ensure clear roles and responsibilities for senior managers for operational risk management, business continuity and service provider arrangements.

**Paragraph 26(b):** entities must identify and document the processes and resources needed to deliver critical operations, "including people, technology, information, facilities and service providers".
**Paragraphs 28 and 29:** internal controls must be designed, implemented and embedded, then regularly monitored, reviewed and tested for design and operating effectiveness.
**Paragraph 31:** operational risk incidents and near misses must be identified, escalated, recorded and addressed in a timely manner.
**Paragraph 40:** entities must maintain the capabilities required to execute the business continuity plan (BCP), "including access to people, resources and technology".
**Paragraph 42:** the BCP testing program must include an annual business continuity exercise testing the plan against severe but plausible scenarios.

blocks.text: A search of the 2026 standard and the 2026 CPG 230 finds no use of the word training. APRA leaves the means to the entity, which makes a structured [training needs analysis](/glossary/training-needs-analysis) against these paragraphs a practical way to decide what people need.

sections.heading: How can training evidence CPS 230 compliance?

blocks.text: Training evidence is most useful when each CPS 230 duty is linked to a named role, a learning outcome and an artifact a supervisor or auditor can inspect. The table below is an original, illustrative mapping; it is not APRA guidance.

blocks.text: Key person dependency is a direct CPS 230 issue: if only one person can execute a critical BCP step, paragraph 40 capability is fragile. A [skills matrix](/glossary/skills-matrix) showing trained alternates for each critical role is simple evidence that capability does not rest on one individual.
Staff who detect or escalate events need to know that APRA's clocks start when the entity becomes aware, not when a report reaches the risk team. The 2026 standard sets these deadlines:

blocks.text: CPG 230 notes that an information security incident notified under CPS 234 does not need to be separately reported under CPS 230. The information security side is covered in [CPS 234 security awareness training](/regulations/apra-cps-234-security-awareness-training).

sections.heading: What should a CPS 230 capability program include?

blocks.text: A proportionate program starts from the register of critical operations and works out who must do what under the BCP, controls framework and incident process. A workable sequence:

items: List the roles named in the operational risk framework, BCP and service provider policy.
For each role, state the CPS 230 paragraph it supports and the observable capability required.
Assess current capability and identify single points of failure.
Build short, role specific modules and exercises rather than one generic course.
Use the annual business continuity exercise and control testing results as assessment evidence.
Feed incidents and near misses back into content, as paragraph 31 requires them to inform the risk profile.
Report capability coverage for critical operations to the Board alongside tolerance monitoring.

blocks.text: The guide to [reporting training compliance to the board](/guides/how-to-report-training-compliance-to-the-board) covers how to present this without turning it into a completion statistic.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links CPS 230 paragraphs, an entity's critical operations and its BCP roles in one framework, so each role's required capability and assessment point is explicit. When APRA amends the standard, as it did in 2026, the affected roles and materials can be found from the framework rather than by manual review.

faqs.q: Does CPS 230 require annual operational risk training?
faqs.a: No. CPS 230 does not mention training or set a frequency. It does require an annual business continuity exercise (paragraph 42) and regular control testing (paragraph 29), which many entities use as the main evidence that people can perform their roles.

faqs.q: Did CPS 230 replace CPS 232 and CPS 231?
faqs.a: Yes. CPS 230 replaced the earlier business continuity and outsourcing standards. For non-significant financial institutions, the existing business continuity requirements continued to apply until June 30, 2026 because the CPS 230 continuity paragraphs were deferred to July 1, 2026.

The deferred business continuity requirements began to apply to non-significant financial institutions, the transition for pre-existing service provider contracts ended, and APRA's remade CPS 230 with limited exemptions for certain service provider categories commenced alongside an updated CPG 230.

faqs.q: Who is accountable for operational risk capability?
faqs.a: The Board is ultimately accountable for oversight of operational risk management under paragraph 19, and must ensure clear roles and responsibilities for senior managers under paragraph 20. Those senior managers are the natural owners of capability for their operations.
